Plot a GO-Term Overlap Network

Source: R/network_plots.R
plot_network.Rd

Draws one or more views of a network built by generate_overlap_network (or run_comparison_networks / recluster_network). All types except themes share the layout stored in the network result, so nodes sit in the same place in each.

Usage

plot_network(
  net_result,
  type = "leiden",
  label_by = c("ancestor", "keywords", "phrase", "hub"),
  min_terms = 3,
  title = NULL,
  outdir = NULL,
  file_stem = NULL
)

Arguments

net_result

A scoranet_network object from generate_overlap_network, run_comparison_networks or recluster_network.

type

Character. One or more of:

"leiden" (default)

Nodes filled by Leiden cluster, with the cluster legend on the left.

"regulation"

Nodes filled by direction: up, down, or mixed.

"zscore"

Nodes filled by a continuous blue-white-red gradient of the direction score (a descriptive score, not a statistical test). Needs direction scores in the network (see build_network_inputs).

"themes"

The Leiden plot annotated with cluster themes: a shaded hull around each cluster with a callout naming its theme, and a layout that keeps each cluster together (so node positions differ from the other plots).

"all"

All four.

In regulation, leiden and themes, node shape shows direction (circle = up in ident1, square = up in ident2, diamond = mixed). Edge width shows Jaccard overlap; node size shows the number of DE genes in the term.

label_by

Character. Text used to label each cluster in the themes plot:

"ancestor" (default)

Up to theme_max_ancestors higher-level GO terms that the cluster's terms fall under in the GO hierarchy (via GO.db), with how many of the cluster's terms they cover, e.g. "cytokine production / response to cytokine (22/39)". Falls back to the hub term when no ancestor qualifies or the results have no GO IDs.

"keywords"

The most distinctive words in the cluster's term names.

"phrase"

The top term name, as used by the wordclouds.

"hub"

The cluster's most connected term.

min_terms

Integer. In the themes plot, clusters with fewer terms get a hull but no callout label, to limit clutter. They are still listed colour-coded in the cluster legend. Default 3.

title

Character plot title. If NULL (default), the title is the network's collection_name plus the plot type, e.g. "<name> (Leiden)". A title given here is used for every type.

outdir

Character path to an output directory. If non-NULL, each plot is saved as a PNG along with the CSV tables it shows (see Side effects). The directory is created if it does not exist; a trailing / is optional. Default NULL (nothing is written).

file_stem

Character filename prefix. Defaults to the file_stem stored in net_result.

Value

One ggplot object when one type is drawn, otherwise a named list of ggplot objects. zscore is skipped (with a message) when the network has no direction scores and other types are requested; asking for zscore alone is then an error.

Side effects

When outdir is set, each plot is saved as <file_stem>-regulation.png, -clustered-leiden.png, -zscore.png or -themes.png, and the network_tables behind it are saved as CSVs in the same folder:

regulationsummary, membership
leidensummary, cluster_stats, membership
zscoresummary, membership
themessummary, cluster_stats, membership, themes

Each CSV is written once per call.

See also

generate_overlap_network, recluster_network, network_tables
